reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch argue Jeremiah's seventy years carries symbolic rather than strict arithmetical weight, easing its clash with Baruch's seven generations.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg lists Jeremiah's seventy-year captivity among the Bible's many sacred-number sevens, reading it as schematic rather than a literal count.

quotes.text: Seventy was a sacred number with the Jews and is of frequent occurrence in their writings … Jeremiah prophesied that the Jews were to “serve the king of Babylon seventy years” (xxv, 11).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on Jeremiah 25:11.

sides.snippet: these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years
sides.verseText: This whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

sides.snippet: After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I will visit you
sides.verseText: For thus says Yahweh, After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
